away.name: Logan Thompson
away.news: Thompson will start Tuesday in Tampa.

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Vasilevskiy, the reigning Vezina Trophy winner, has been far from stellar this season. That said, he played well in his most recent outing, saving 20 of 21 shots (.952 SV%), but his team let him down in a 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings. The 32-year-old goalie has uncharacteristically allowed three or more goals in nine of 15 games this season (9-5-1). Still, Tampa Bay enters Tuesday's game as -154 home favourites against a Washington Capitals team that has been outscored 12-6 in their past two games (0-2-0).

away.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
away.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has struggled to start his tenure with the Maple Leafs, posting an ugly 3.47 GAA and .881 SV% in 13 games (3-8-2). Even more alarming, Bobrovsky has allowed three or more goals in all but one of his 13 outings. The veteran 38-year-old goalie hopes to snap a five-game losing streak on Tuesday, as the Maple Leafs enter action as -146 road favourites against the league's worst offence, the Chicago Blackhawks (2.3 GF/GP).

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: After a promising inaugural full season with the Blackhawks in 2025-26, posting a 2.82 GAA and .902 SV% in 55 games (19-25-11), Knight has had an inconsistent start to 2026-27. In his most recent game, he allowed four goals on 31 shots (.871 SV%) in a 5-4 shootout loss to the Winnipeg Jets. The 25-year-old American goalie has allowed four or more goals in four of his last five games (1-3-1). The Blackhawks enter Tuesday's game as +133 home underdogs against a struggling Toronto Maple Leafs team that is desperately trying to snap a six-game losing streak (0-6-0).

away.name: Ville Husso
away.news: Husso led the Ducks onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Jordan Binnington
home.news: After a career-worst 2025-26 season, posting a 3.33 GAA and .873 SV% in 41 games (13-20-7), Binnington has struggled to start 2026-27, taking a clear backseat to Joel Hofer. The 33-year-old Binnington has only had one quality start in five games this season (1-3-0) and has allowed five or more goals three times. The Blues enter Tuesday's game as -128 home favourites against the Anaheim Ducks, who are coming off an explosive 6-1 win over the Calgary Flames.

away.name: Justus Annunen
away.news: Annunen will start Tuesday in Minnesota.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has deservedly been the busiest goalie in the NHL this season, playing 19 of 22 games, posting a tremendous 1.94 GAA and .926 SV% with a 14-2-3 record. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie was excellent in Minnesota's previous game, saving 31 of 33 shots (.939 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Boston Bruins. With Filip Gustavsson (hip) nearing his season debut, Wallstedt will likely see a slightly lighter workload, but he has proven himself as one of the NHL's best goalies on any given night. Minnesota enters Tuesday's game as -196 home favourites against a Nashville Predators team whose seven-game winning streak was snapped on Sunday in a 4-2 loss to the San Jose Sharks.

away.name: Jake Oettinger
away.news: Oettinger was stellar in his most recent game, stopping all 22 shots he faced to lead a 2-0 shutout win over the Buffalo Sabres. That said, the 27-year-old Oettinger has been wildly inconsistent this season. Oettinger leads the NHL with four shutouts, but has a sub- .900 SV% in seven of 15 games this season (10-4-1). The Stars enter Tuesday's game as +109 road underdogs against a Vegas Golden Knights team coming off a disappointing 6-3 loss to the Vancouver Canucks.

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have had a liberal goalie rotation in recent weeks and will continue that trend on Tuesday, turning to Adin Hill. After posting a career-worst 3.04 GAA and .871 SV% in 27 games last season (10-9-6), Hill has bounced back, posting a 2.47 GAA and .908 SV% in 10 games (7-2-1). He has a 1.62 GAA and a .943 SV% in his last three games (2-0-1). The Golden Knights enter Thursday's game as -130 home favourites against the Dallas Stars, who are 5-1-1 in their last seven games.

away.name: Dustin Wolf
away.news: Before being sidelined with a lower-body injury, Devin Cooley owned the crease in Calgary, but he has struggled since returning. Meanwhile, Dustin Wolf seems to have found his game during Cooley's absence. The 25-year-old Wolf was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 29 of 31 shots (.935 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Los Angeles Kings. In his last five games (3-1-1), Wolf has a solid 2.22 GAA and a .920 SV%. The Flames enter Tuesday's game as +116 road underdogs against the San Jose Sharks, whom they defeated 2-1 earlier this month.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov had a rough performance in his previous outing, allowing five goals on 32 shots (.844 SV%), but managed to win 6-5 in a shootout over the Utah Mammoth. The 24-year-old Russian goalie has had an inconsistent season. In 15 games this season (6-8-1), Askarov has allowed four or more goals six times, but has allowed two or fewer seven times. The Sharks enter Tuesday's game as -127 home favourites against a Calgary Flames team coming off a 6-1 loss to the Anaheim Ducks.
